title: "Introduction"
format: html

Growth is a dynamic process in which the size, mass, concentration, or other measurable characteristic of a biological system changes over time.

Sigmoidal growth models summarize an entire trajectory using a small number of parameters related to characteristics such as:

- asymptotic response;
- growth rate;
- timing of the inflection point;
- symmetry or shape of the trajectory.

PGM provides a graphical interface for fitting these models in jamovi, while retaining statistical procedures commonly implemented in R.

## Why use parametric growth models?

Parametric growth models can provide interpretable summaries of nonlinear trajectories. Depending on the selected model, their parameters may describe:

- the expected mature or asymptotic value;
- the temporal scale of growth;
- the maximum growth rate;
- the age or time of maximum growth rate;
- the shape and asymmetry of the curve.

These interpretations depend on the equation and parametrization used. Parameters with similar names are not necessarily equivalent across different growth models.

## Statistical challenges

Biological growth data frequently present characteristics that are not adequately represented by ordinary nonlinear least squares, including:

- increasing or decreasing residual variability;
- repeated observations from the same experimental unit;
- between-individual variation in growth parameters;
- serial correlation between observations;
- incomplete or irregular measurement schedules.

PGM therefore includes variance functions, nonlinear mixed-effects models, and residual correlation structures.

## Documentation conventions

Throughout this documentation:

- $W(t)$ denotes the fitted growth function;
- $W'(t)$ denotes the instantaneous growth rate;
- $W''(t)$ denotes growth acceleration;
- $t$ denotes time or age;
- $y$ denotes the observed response.

The interpretation of each model-specific parameter is presented in the chapter on growth models.
